name: Hampshire Controls Corporation
old_description: Established in 1976 and based in Dover, New Hampshire, Hampshire Controls is a leading designer and manufacturer of supremely reliable “Made in the USA” monitoring, logging, and alert status notification systems for demanding applications.
about:
Hampshire Controls Corporation was established in 1976 in Dover, New Hampshire, where it remains headquartered. The company began as a designer and manufacturer of monitoring, logging, and alert status notification systems, emphasizing "Made in the USA" reliability for demanding applications.

The firm designs and produces a range of NIST-traceable calibrated instruments, including temperature monitors and alarms for blood and plasma, cryogenic temperature monitors, multi-probe condition monitors, data logging and alarm systems, Wi-Fi temperature transmitters, biomedical freezer backup systems (liquid CO2 and liquid nitrogen), liquid nitrogen level monitors, and laboratory air flow monitors. Engineering, manufacturing, testing, and calibration are performed in-house at the Dover facility, covering PCB soldering, cable manufacturing, subsystem interfacing, final electronic assembly, firmware development, and custom enclosure design.

Hampshire Controls serves blood banks, vaccine and genetic research laboratories, biopharma production facilities, governmental agencies, hospitals, commercial food processing and storage operations, and industrial manufacturing firms. The company works directly with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), government agencies, research laboratories, and industrial customers, supplying both standard and custom-engineered products for applications such as blood product verification, cryogenic storage monitoring, and environmental condition logging.

The company differentiates itself through its U.S.-based design and manufacturing, NIST-traceable calibration services, and the ability to deliver fully custom systems — from mechanical and electrical engineering through firmware, testing, and calibration — under one roof. Its products carry UL Listing, and the firm holds a U.S. government CAGE code (0H2P8) for federal procurement.

name: Hanley's Foods
old_description: Hanley’s makes premium, natural salad dressings with a taste of Louisiana.
about:
Founded in 2010 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, Hanley's Foods began as a salad-loving venture by Richard and Kate Hanley, who launched their first dressing at the Red Stick Farmer's Market in 2012 after discovering their favorite restaurant-style dressing was unavailable in stores. The couple, together since high school, refined their recipe through family taste tests before partnering with the LSU AgCenter's Food Incubator to bring the product to market.

The company produces premium, all-natural salad dressings and croutons from scratch at its Louisiana facility, using locally sourced ingredients. Hanley's focuses exclusively on these two product lines, manufacturing every bottle in-house. Today its products are stocked in more than 2,000 retail locations across the United States, including major chains such as Walmart, Costco, Whole Foods, and regional grocers like Rouses Markets.

Hanley's serves the retail grocery sector and foodservice operators, with customers ranging from national big-box retailers to hospitality groups such as Compass Group and Royal Caribbean. The company also offers wholesale partnerships for independent grocers and specialty stores.

The founders say their differentiation lies in a single-minded commitment to quality: premium natural ingredients, Louisiana-made production, and adherence to rigorous food-safety standards including HACCP, NSF, SQF, GMP, and supporting programs such as SOP, SSOP, CCP, and CAP.

name: Hansen Plastics Corporation
old_description: Hansen Plastics Corporation: Plastic Manufacturers in Illinois & Custom Injection Molding Services
about:
Hansen Plastics Corporation operates from Elgin, Illinois, where it was founded in 1971 by Elmer Hansen. The company transitioned to an Employee Stock Ownership Plan in 1991 and became 100% employee-owned by 1998, a structure the firm says embeds a "do it right the first time" tradition into daily operations.

The shop runs more than 70 injection molding presses ranging from 28 to 500 tons across over 150,000 square feet of production space. Core processes include horizontal, vertical/insert, multi-material, and decoupled molding, supported by RJG scientific molding with cavity-pressure transducers. Value-added services span in-mold decorating, hot stamping, pad printing, machining, tapping, turning, drilling, ultrasonic welding, thermal insertion, hand assembly, and custom packaging. The company handles volumes from prototypes to high‑volume runs.

Customers include OEMs and manufacturers across North America in automotive, life safety, appliances, fluid movement and water treatment, construction, transportation (non‑automotive), agriculture, and water filtration. Testimonials cite long‑term relationships with buyers in automotive tooling and water delivery equipment.

Leadership attributes the company’s differentiation to its employee‑owner culture, ISO 9001:2015 certification, lean manufacturing practices, and statistical process controls tied to business systems. The founder, Elmer Hansen, remains on the board, reinforcing the original quality motto.

name: Happy's Gifts and Apparel

about:
Happy's Gifts and Apparel operates from Hazen, North Dakota, in Mercer County. The business was started about five years ago by Keith and Morgan, a husband-and-wife team who moved from nearby Washburn to be closer to their growing customer base. Keith, a paramedic with over a decade of experience, and Morgan run the shop as a Christian, family-owned, home-based operation.

The company provides custom embroidery, laser engraving and cutting, branded apparel (t-shirts, polos, hats), insulated stainless-steel tumblers, and a range of promotional products such as keychains, coozies, awards, and magnets. They work with materials including wood, leather, acrylic, and fabric, using a laser engraver and an embroidery machine. The shop handles orders from small batches to wholesale volumes of 10–100+ pieces, offering free design proofs and bulk pricing.

Happy's serves local businesses and organizations across Mercer County, including oil field crews, schools, churches, farms, and event organizers in Hazen, Beulah, Stanton, and surrounding communities. They produce embroidered uniforms for work teams, laser-engraved awards for events, custom tumblers for client gifts, and branded apparel for employee recognition and tradeshows.

The founders emphasize a personal, hands-on approach—customers work directly with the people making the products—and a commitment to keeping dollars in the community. They position themselves as a one-stop local alternative to out-of-state online vendors, offering fast turnaround, local pickup, and wholesale rates with flexible minimums.

The firm serves customers in the ornamental iron, miscellaneous metal, and structural steel sectors, primarily performing subcontracted fabrication for other contractors and project owners. Concrete client names are not disclosed in public materials.

The company states that its founding vision was to deliver the highest quality fabricated structural steel that meets or exceeds project expectations, a commitment summarized as consistent, reliable, and cost-effective service. name: Haven Steel Products Inc
old_description: Haven Steel Products began construction of its production facility in 1968 and has been a privately-owned company producing spring steel components since 1969. Our company fabricates, and heat treats components for the agricultural industry (tillage components), the construction industry (landscaping and mowing components), the trailer industry (leaf springs), and many other clients.
about:
Haven Steel Products began building its production facility in Haven, Kansas, in 1968 and started producing spring steel components the following year. The privately owned company was founded as a fabricator for the agricultural, construction, and trailer industries, and has since expanded to a second plant in McKenzie, Tennessee.

The company operates more than 200,000 square feet of production space across its two sites, offering forging on presses up to 1,000 tons, hot forming with natural gas and induction furnaces, eight quench-and-temper heat-treat lines, powder coating, a 30 kW fiber laser with bevel capability, in-house tooling, CNC machining, and a growing fleet of Kuka robots. Recent investments include two 700-ton forging presses, a 36-inch belt furnace, a Flex CNC, and a 34,000-square-foot warehouse in Kansas.

Haven Steel supplies heat-treated and tempered components to major OEMs and short-line manufacturers in agriculture (tillage parts, rotary cutter blades), construction (landscaping and mowing components), trailer (leaf springs, weight-equalizing hitch springs), railroad (wear plates), recycling (chopper knives), grounds keeping (aerator knives), playground equipment, and patio furniture.

The company emphasizes full traceability from raw steel through every process, maintains an ISO 9001:2015 quality system with ASM and FEMA membership, and holds calibration records for a minimum of three years. Its proprietary Ultra Tuf Coatings™ slurry coating is said to extend the service life of wear parts by three to five times.
